value.hook: Before changing daemon-log EOF handling or grading buffered-read preservation
value.title: R326 EOF closure preserves sink newline framing

sections.name: body
sections.value:
R326 FINAL R2 c8d3905 closes R326-001; governed PASS c343ef19. EOF now writes a nonempty vector retained across timeout through Shared::line before finish. The newline is the existing stamp convention for every unterminated fragment, not a new format; the stream-local buffer and unchanged output index preserve sink routing. In-repo readers use newline timestamps/.lines() or raw log capture, with no special meaning for an unterminated logger line. The repaired logger and watchdog files were unchanged by the main merge.

Proof: all23 shipped logger tests plus original3s production-bound EOF and continuation controls passed25/25. Removing only EOF write failed both shipped20ms regression and original EOF oracle; continuation stayedgreen. Exact restoration checked, focusedrepeat3/3green. CI artifact14719649092:2838 cases, no errors/failures,23 logger unit+5 integration. No new finding/notes owed. R1 watchdog scope/lifecycle proof carries over; R2 adds only the final sink write, no loop/launch. Local TS gates remain dependency-limited, notgreen.

MagicWand: preservation must be asserted at the sink, not inferred from a retained Vec. Keep EOF and continuation negative controls together. For mutants of tests that panic before deleting fixtures, set TMPDIR to an owned archive subdirectory at launch; fresh_dir reads std::env::temp_dir and includes process id, nanos and counter. Then failure cleanup stays confined to that owned tree (F262), never a machine-wide prefix sweep. Logs/patches retained in session files; source+temp archive cleaned after all children exited.
